anti_overlap: Cathedral focuses on cross-generational handoff and load-bearing decision sequencing; differs from heraldry which examines whether identity-specification grammar is transmissible
Cathedral examines the build-sequence and stone-course commitments; differs from glacier which examines accumulated event history and selective forgetting
Cathedral cares about successors' ability to continue; raga focuses on whether improvisation remains recognisable within fixed scaffolding
decision_lens: Does this brainstorm specify the engine in a way that a successor team — picking it up after the original authors are gone, distracted, or burned out — could continue without re-deciding the foundational geometry?
distance_rationale: Pre-modern construction tradition with documented multi-generational handoff problems is structurally analogous to a software engine spanning years and possible team turnover, but draws from a discipline entirely outside software/games.
expected_isomorphisms: Cathedral master-builders solved the problem of how a half-built vault transmits its design-intent to masons two generations later through stone-by-stone constraint propagation and explicit course-by-course gates. The Palettice migration faces an isomorphic challenge: how does Phase 1's stone course constrain Phase 4's vault without freezing the design space, and what is the equivalent of the working drawing that lets a successor continue without re-deciding the foundational geometry?
focus: Whether the brainstorm's multi-decade engine ambition is structured for completion by successors, not by current authors
name: fd-cathedral-cross-generational-engineering
persona: Apply the perspective of a medieval cathedral master-builder tradition — they care about whether a design can be paused, handed off, and resumed correctly across generations of builders, whether the working drawings transmit intent without the original author present, and whether load-bearing geometry stays buildable when masons centuries later inherit the half-finished crossing.
review_areas: Whether the migration plan encodes intent in artifacts (FacetCataloguePolicy, ArchetypeDerivation configs) rather than in the heads of current contributors
Whether Phase 1's stone-course (Soul + SoulStore + derivations) constrains Phases 2-4 enough that out-of-sequence work cannot collapse the vault
Whether the §Open Questions are framed as decidable-later (with clear inputs) or as latent ambiguity that will silently re-decide itself
Whether the convergence claim ('three projects, one engine') is documented as a falsifiable structural drawing or as a master-builder's verbal lore
Whether the Culture-game horizon — explicitly years out — has been translated into stone-course gates that the migration MVP cannot accidentally pour over
Whether deferred decisions (extraction shape, timescale, Culture-as-Soul) are anchored by load-bearing constraints that prevent later builders from choosing incompatibly

severity_examples.condition: The shadow-work-as-reference commitment depends on undocumented knowledge of which of shadow-work's 31 facets are load-bearing vs. accidental; a successor migrating Phase 2 cannot tell which decisions are structural and which are scaffolding
severity_examples.scenario: Migration sequence assumes implicit shared context

severity_examples.condition: Open Questions 1-6 list options but do not specify what evidence from migration experience would resolve them, making it impossible for a later author to recognise when the question has become answerable
severity_examples.scenario: Open Questions left without decision-input specs

severity_examples.condition: The 'three projects converged on one engine' claim is stated as recognition but the structural overlap is not enumerated facet-by-facet, so a successor cannot verify the isomorphism is real vs. coincidental shape-matching

success_hints: Treat the brainstorm as a working drawing for builders who do not share the current authors' tacit knowledge
Distinguish load-bearing structural commitments from scaffolding that will be torn down
Ask whether each deferred decision has a clear gate condition for being decided later
Look for the equivalent of 'plinth courses' — early commitments that constrain everything above them
task_context: The brainstorm proposes a multi-year engine evolution (Palettice Phase 1 → Culture-game endpoint) with explicit acknowledgement that the Culture game may never be built and that intermediate work must justify itself anyway. Reviewing whether the document equips future contributors — possibly different humans, possibly without the original authors' context — to continue the work coherently.
